title: Surgical revert prober for multi-signal canaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current canary automation at Redwood relies on single-threshold triggers (p95/p99 latency or error rate) which either fire too late or create noisy rollbacks for traffic-sensitive customers. We need an automated controller that is sensitive to multi-dimensional SLO regressions (latency tail, error rate, token cost, throughput) while minimizing false positives and enabling surgical, partial reverts instead of full evacuations.

Goal: Build a 'Surgical Revert Prober' — an orchestration component that continuously probes canary cohorts, fuses signals across SLOs and cohorts, and recommends/executes staged traffic surgery (slice-level weight adjustments and model fallback) with a tunable hysteresis model. The prober should: (1) detect regressions early with bounded false positive rate, (2) provide human-readable justification for actions, (3) support graduated rollback actions (shadow fade, route-to-fallback, reduce weight by X%), and (4) allow per-customer and per-route sensitivity profiles.

Design summary:
- Multi-signal fusion: compute independent baseline deltas for p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, per-token cost volatility, and throughput. Each signal is normalized to a cohort-specific z-score using rolling-window mean+variance.
- Change detection: use a two-stage detector: fast EWMA-based short-window detector for early warning + Bayesian posterior change test over a longer window for confirmation. Only confirmed signals trigger automated surgery unless configured for aggressive early-eject.
- Cohort-aware baselines: cohorts are defined by route, customer tier, and input sequence length bucket. Baselines are decay-updated and snapshotted pre-rollout for drift-insensitive comparisons.
- Adaptive thresholds: thresholds are tuned relative to observed variance and effective N. We use a configurable alpha (default 0.01) and minimum effect size threshold to avoid reacting to trivial percentage changes at high volume.
- Action model (graduated):
  * Stage 0: annotate + notify (no action) for low-confidence signals
  * Stage 1: reduce canary weight by percentage (e.g., -30%) and enable extra tracing on affected slices
  * Stage 2: route matching cohort to documented fallback model variant (quantized or cheaper variant) for a portion of traffic
  * Stage 3: full evacuation of canary model (last resort)
- Hysteresis and cooldowns: actions have minimum hold times and exponential backoff on re-escalation. Re-introduction requires passing confirmation windows.
- Observability: every decision emits structured trace events (reason, contributing signals, confidence, pre/post metrics) and a human-friendly summary for Console. Dashboards show per-cohort signal contribution and the suggested action.

Trade-offs considered:
- Statistical rigor vs. latency to action: conservative confirmatory tests reduce false positives but delay mitigation; we adopt two-stage detector to balance.
- Complexity vs. transparency: multi-signal fusion can be opaque; we commit to generating ranked contributors and a natural-language rationale for each automated action.
- Per-customer sensitivity: high-SLA customers can opt into stricter or looser controllers; default profile aims for platform-wide balance.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype detector library (Go) that takes time-series vectors and returns ranked anomalies + confidence. (Spike: 2 sprints)
2) Integrate with rollout controller to expose action plan and dry-run mode where suggestions are logged but not applied. (1 sprint)
3) Implement staged action executor that manipulates traffic weights and fallbacks via existing routing APIs. (1 sprint)
4) Console UX: rollout timeline, decision transcript, and manual override buttons. (1 sprint)
5) Canaries -> gradual opt-in with Beta customers and synthetic traffic harness for stress testing.

Success criteria:
- Reduce full-model evacuations by 60% across canary launches in the first month post-launch (measured vs last 6 months).
- False positive automated actions rate < 5% of all automated suggestions (requires human review sampling).
- Time-to-mitigate median reduced by 40% for confirmed regressions.

Testing & rollout: start with internal canaries + synthetic regressions, then opt-in Beta orgs, then platform default with opt-out.

Notes: This ticket covers the core detection+action model and Console transcripts; separate tickets will cover advanced per-customer policy editor and integrations with dedicated capacity billing signals for token-cost SLOs.
